title: MZ Of course my scope is too far out!

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
Summary: Game development can be quite
difficult
.
I'm trying to add some more graphics and interactivity to my project with RPG Maker MZ,
Three.JS
, and
Rapier
. I know MZ3D is already a plugin using Babylon.js and Chaucer has the Rose engine, but I've been using Three.js since around 2016 for 3D. It was the industry standard for a long time. I recently ran into Rapier which will allow me to use a physics engine with RPG Maker in 3D. Other devs told me to use Godot, Unity, or Unreal, but I refused. I took a look and it would be fastest with RPG Maker. It doesn't add any additional work because I would still need to setup the foundation. I will have to have some 3rd party level editor like the notes that CutieVirus setup with MZ3D, but I was thinking of something like a JSON or XML file. Crafting in the notes section is difficult without instant feedback or a WYSIWYG editor. Maybe make a tool like an RPG Maker 3D editor assistant?
Graphical issues
I am in pre-alpha stage. Any criticisms about how I'm designing or programming this are non-offensive because it isn't done yet; like criticizing air
. I am developing an action RPG, but I find the collision detection slightly off. The timing would throw players for a loop for blocking, parrying, and counters. There is about a 1-2 square time issue rather than 5 frames or 10 pixels. I'm hoping to clean it up. I have to completely change the collision detection, but to do that, I have to change the animation and rendering. I'm adding a
Spriter Pro
with the
plugin
to fix the FPS issue. I'll have to update the plugin or ask Kana if he could update for MZ. For the prototype, I am still using the RTP, but I'm going to switch to either tall, pre-rendered, or 3D characters. I have run into a mess of issues. Devices not rendering WebGL on basic laptops, phones saying they can't render primitives in an APK, but it can on a shader website, and Linux/Mac not supporting my protocols without doing some roundabouts. Right now, I'm getting less than 12 FPS on the test laptop with only a cloud rendering; that's unacceptable for my players. If I run it on my gaming computer, it is more than 120 FPS. If I can't get the 3D to work then I'm going to use pre-rendered 3D. I have barely thought about mode 7 or parallax with this.
I also want to bring in shaders into RPG Maker. They look nice and makes it easier to make good looking games.
Any suggestions for graphics, performance enhancement, or optimization would be appreciated!
Physics issues
After an enemy or a character is hit back, the physics is clumsy. It is a push back around 50 pixels from the attack and plays the animation with sound. My interrupts to attacks are primitive. Player charges for a lightning bolt at 200 px while an enemy dashes or shoots a fireball and the enemy gets the hit. Fire doesn't fire, ice doesn't ice, bolt doesn't bolt, but quake does quake! I'm not making a physics engine like Black Desert Online, just a cute little physics engine about as sophisticated as a 2000-2008 game. I enjoy when players walk through the jungle and the plants sway back as the party goes deeper, or water ripples as they sprint down the beaches from a hoard of monsters, or they are trekking across the mountain tops as snow prints are left behind with their shadows; physics-y stuff. I'm sure some players don't really mind, while Chrono Trigger had little physics, it is one of the greatest RPGs of all time to me. Those little somethings that give players spectacular experiences.
If you can think of small details of like forensics or physics that make the game better, leave a note please.
Player issues
I like my games hard, usually near impossible hard, but that is not for most audiences. The difficulty is too hard to start. I might have crafted the RPG Maker version of Dark Souls. I'm experimenting with adaptive difficulties using
GameAnalytics.js
. My initial assumption is ±15% difficulty should be fine, if not then they should drop the difficulty to prevent rage inducing situations. By the time I have an alpha, the difficulty will be under control. Increased difficulty will increase the reward percentage. If you have a thorough knowledge of event listeners with player analytics, please give me some hints.
I haven't found the perfect difficulty. What is the perfect difficulty? I've seen the charts. Player flow state, average person IQ, and technology adaption rates. It is difficult to describe the fun in difficulty. Even when it is fun, there needs to be the right amount of rewards.
I'm just going to make a great game.

posts.author: TRIDIUM
posts.body:
I'm a bit curious, how did you arrive at the decision to use RPG Maker to make a 3d action game? With physics. And shaders.
Making an ARPG in RPG Maker is like trying to fit a square peg in a circular hole. It can be done, but it's not gonna be fun. You're trying to fit all the shapes in the same hole at the same time.
DrFreeman said:
I might have crafted the RPG Maker version of Dark Souls
Click to expand...
I'm sure you just used that comparison because it's well known, but it does irk me a bit when people distill the souls series to just its difficulty. There's a lot more going on in the game, and the difficulty is very specifically designed and handled. 99% of "soulslikes" mess the difficulty up because of the mindset that it should be artificially hard.

posts.author: lianderson
posts.body:
If you're using RPG maker, I suggest you drop the 3d action altogether and just focus on what made chrono trigger special to you. I'm not saying copy it, I'm just saying, figure out what it did and go from there.
You got a long journey ahead of you. Good luck.

posts.body: You can't use that chart for player IQ. You have to assume they're f****** dumb. I've had several people complain/rage that my game would need skip options, even though it does have that and its said on download page, beginning of game and when first gameplay segment starts.

posts.author: Arcaines
posts.body:
rpgLord69 said:
You can't use that chart for player IQ. You have to assume they're f****** dumb. I've had several people complain/rage that my game would need skip options, even though it does have that and its said on download page, beginning of game and when first gameplay segment starts.

I've had a player who couldn't get past my title screen and said it was stuck there.
So I had to add a Press space bar to continue prompt.
Now back to the topic at hand I'm going to mention the difficulty and player IQ part.
First, there is no such thing as perfect difficulty. Some players like their easy games whilst others like their super duper hard games. There is no perfect middle.
And using the average player IQ isn't something you should be using. A Persons IQ would have no impact on how they play a game.
Knowledge about the game is gained from playing the game and how people adapt to it regardless of IQ.
IQ's are not a universal  to everything.
